_source: TimeBank-Dense annotation guidelines, Cassidy, McDowell, Chambers & Bethard, 'An Annotation Framework for Dense Event Ordering', ACL 2014 (short), https://aclanthology.org/P14-2082/. Label inventory verbatim from Section 3.1.1 ('6 relations: before, after, includes, is included, simultaneous, and vague') and footnote 4 ('a relation like starts is a special case of includes if events are viewed as open intervals, and immediately before is a special case of before'). The 80% confidence rule, the modal/conditional rule, the aspectual rule, the property-attribution rule and the generic-event rule are quoted from Section 3.2 (p. 504) without the paper's example sentences; the 80% rule is changed from 'annotators ... if they are 80% confident' to second person and given its VAGUE consequence (Section 3.2: majority rule 'otherwise it is marked VAGUE'). The paper gives no per-label definitions; BEFORE/AFTER/INCLUDES/IS_INCLUDED/SIMULTANEOUS descriptions state the TimeML interval semantics the labels name. Label names follow the released data codes (b, a, i, ii, s, v) and ConTempo (Niu et al., Findings ACL 2024) Table 1, which writes SIMULTANEOUS as EQUAL. No test examples are used.

_state_fields.context: the sentence containing both events, or the two consecutive sentences containing them, from an English news article; Event 1's trigger word is wrapped in <e1>...</e1> and Event 2's in <e2>...</e2>

question.instructions: Temporal relation classification between two events in a news text (TimeBank-Dense scheme). The state holds "context": one sentence or two consecutive sentences from an English news article, in which the trigger word of Event 1 is wrapped in <e1>...</e1> and the trigger word of Event 2 is wrapped in <e2>...</e2>; "event_1" and "event_2" repeat the two trigger words. Each trigger stands for the whole event it describes, viewed as a time interval. Choose the relation of Event 1 (<e1>) to Event 2 (<e2>), in that order, from 6 relations: before, after, includes, is included, simultaneous, and vague. A relation like starts is a special case of includes if events are viewed as open intervals, and immediately before is a special case of before. Annotation guidelines: The 80% confidence rule: choose a specific non-vague relation if you are 80% confident that it was the writer's intent that a reader infer that relation; otherwise the relation is VAGUE. Modal and conditional events: interpreted with a possible worlds analysis. The core event was treated as having occurred, whether or not the text implied that it had occurred. Negated events and hypotheticals are treated similarly. One assumes the event does occur, and all other events are ordered accordingly. Aspectual events: annotated as IS INCLUDED in their event arguments. For instance, events that describe the manner in which another event is performed are considered encompassed by the broader event. Events that attribute a property to a person or event are interpreted to end when the entity ends. Generic events can be ordered with respect to each other, but must be VAGUE with respect to nearby non-generic events.

criteria.BEFORE: BEFORE: Event 1 happens before Event 2; Event 1 ends before Event 2 begins (including immediately before).
criteria.AFTER: AFTER: Event 1 happens after Event 2; Event 1 begins after Event 2 ends (including immediately after).
criteria.INCLUDES: INCLUDES: the time interval of Event 1 contains the time interval of Event 2; Event 2 happens during Event 1 (including Event 2 starting or ending Event 1).
criteria.IS_INCLUDED: IS_INCLUDED: the time interval of Event 1 is contained in the time interval of Event 2; Event 1 happens during Event 2 (including Event 1 starting or ending Event 2).
criteria.SIMULTANEOUS: SIMULTANEOUS: Event 1 and Event 2 occupy the same time interval; they happen at the same time.
criteria.VAGUE: VAGUE: no specific relation above can be chosen with 80% confidence that it was the writer's intent that a reader infer it; the text leaves the temporal relation between the two events underspecified.
